title: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra & Ors
facts: This case is a landmark judgment on the scope and ambit of Section 438 of the CrPC, which deals with the grant of anticipatory bail.
The appellant sought anticipatory bail in a case involving charges under Section 302 (Murder) and other sections of the IPC.
The core concern was the balance between the power of the State to investigate and the fundamental right to personal liberty under Article 21.
issues: Whether the High Court or Sessions Court should limit the duration of anticipatory bail.
The criteria and parameters for granting anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC.
The conflict between the rights of the accused and the needs of a fair investigation.
analysis_of_law: Section 438 CrPC: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest.
Article 21 of the Constitution: Protection of life and personal liberty.
Sibbia Case (Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab): The foundational precedent followed here.
precedent_analysis: The Court reaffirmed the principles laid down by the Constitution Bench in the Sibbia case.
It held that there is no requirement in the statute that the accused must make out a 'special case' for anticipatory bail.
courts_reasoning: Personal liberty is a most precious fundamental right. The arrest should be the last option, not the first.
Anticipatory bail is a device to protect the citizen from the humiliation and disgrace of being unnecessarily arrested.
There should be no time limit on the anticipatory bail; it should generally continue till the end of the trial unless cancelled for specific reasons like tampering with evidence.
conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court's refusal and granted anticipatory bail to the appellant.
The judgment provides exhaustive guidelines for judges across the country on how to handle bail applications.
full_ratio: Anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC is a vital safeguard of personal liberty under Article 21. There should be no restrictive conditions like a fixed time limit on such bail. Courts must balance the severity of the crime with the need to protect the individual from arbitrary arrest and harassment.
